items.title: Pay invoice for private land-register entry
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for payment: 01.12.2026 (Tuesday). No weekend/holiday shift needed since it falls on a business day; the date as written is the due date.

warnings: This looks like a well-known German scam pattern: a private commercial company sends an invoice-style letter styled like an official land-registry (Grundbuch) notice for a ‘Grundstückseintrag’, when in fact the German land register is run by the courts (Amtsgericht/Grundbuchamt), not by any private GmbH, and no such payment is ever owed to a private company for your property being in the official Grundbuch.

The letter's own small print admits this is merely a private, unsolicited offer (‘Angebot’) for an entry in the sender's own private directory, unconnected to the official land register (‘steht in keinem Zusammenhang mit dem amtlichen Grundbuch’), and that paying it would create a contract you don't need — do not pay unless you deliberately want this private listing service.

Before sending any money, verify the IBAN's owner matches the sender's exact legal name via your bank's mandatory payee-name check (Empfängerüberprüfung); the IBAN itself is well-formed (DE59 5007 0010 0005 5707 00, Musterbank AG) but a valid IBAN proves nothing about who actually receives the funds.

Consider reporting this letter to consumer-protection bodies (Verbraucherzentrale) or the police, as these schemes are a recognised form of commercial deception (irreführende Geschäftspraktik) against property owners.
